Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC — scheduled 1h
Duration: 54 minutes (recording started at 15:30)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (BlueHarbor), Marcus Rey (BlueHarbor), Priya Kaur (BlueHarbor), Evan Soto (BlueHarbor)
Recording ID: ff-20260304-72b9

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Purpose: scope POC data handling: what we store, redaction, retention policies, and benchmark plan for latency/cost claims.
- Consensus: BlueHarbor wants minimal prompt storage, configurable retention windows, and an initial benchmark scope of 1k queries across 2 prompt families.
- Action: Redwood to run bench, send SOW, security artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): all right thanks everyone for hopping on, uh we're gonna run through a fairly focused agenda today — scope the POC for data handling and benchmarks, make sure success criteria are clear. uh if we can get owners and dates at the end that'd be ideal.
[00:18] Dana (BlueHarbor): thanks Sofia, yeah our main ask is we don't want sensitive customer data sitting around. so redaction and retention are the biggest blockers for compliance. also curious about the telemetry you collect by default.
[00:30] Arjun (Redwood SE): yeah totally, and thanks Dana. quick preview: Redwood's POC can be configured with prompt-avoidance (we call it "minimal prompt storage"), configurable retention windows, and on top we have automatic redaction hooks plus the option to run customer-side redaction before sending. i can show the benchmark design later.
[00:48] Marcus (BlueHarbor): when you say "redaction hooks" do you mean automatic regex-based scrubbers or something more advanced? we need to know what remains in logs for audit.
[01:02] Arjun (Redwood SE): good question. currently we support a combination: configurable regex rules, rule chains for structured forms, and we also provide a post-call review where you can mark tokens for permanent removal. that last bit is more of a manual ops flow but we can automate a lot during the POC. note: automatic redaction is not 100% perfect, so we recommend pre-send redaction for the highest risk fields.
[01:24] Priya (BlueHarbor): to add — we have several prompt types: mortgage intake forms, identity verification snippets, and some free-text support chats. we'd want different retention for each. intake forms might be shorter retention, chat transcripts maybe 90 days, ID verification — ideally never persisted in plaintext.
[01:40] Sofia (Redwood): perfect, that's the kind of granularity we like. for POC success criteria, can we sync on a shortlist? from experience I'd propose: 1) ability to enforce retention window per prompt class, 2) measured latency and cost per 1k queries within agreed SLO, 3) redaction efficacy benchmark (sample of 500 records where sensitive tokens are removed >= 99% per agreed schema) and 4) SSO/KMS proof points for encryption.
[02:14] Dana (BlueHarbor): sounds reasonable. that 99% number on redaction — how do you measure that?
[02:22] Arjun (Redwood SE): we'll run a labeled test set: inject synthetic PII variants across the 500 samples and measure recall/precision of detection + removal. the process: you provide ground-truth labels, we'll run batch through Redwood and compare output. we can share the script and the scoring notebook.
[02:40] Marcus (BlueHarbor): what about telemetry — what do you log by default? we can't have whole prompts in clear text in observability.
[02:50] Arjun (Redwood SE): default telemetry includes token counts, latency percentiles, model variant IDs, error rates, and request metadata like route and region. by default we do not include full prompt text in long-term logs; however short-term request traces for debugging may retain snippets — that is configurable and we can disable snippet capture for the POC.
[03:16] Evan (BlueHarbor): can you support redaction at the edge? our legal wants PII removed before data crosses to vendor.
[03:23] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes, two options: 1) client-side sanitization library you run in your pipeline (we can provide patterns and examples), or 2) private deployment (VPC) where we can run an on-premise package and connect to your KMS. client-side is fastest for POC.
[03:38] Sofia (Redwood): quick check — are you leaning hosted with client-side redaction or private for this pilot?
[03:44] Dana (BlueHarbor): prefer hosted with client-side redaction to start, if the POC goes well we'll eval private.
[03:51] Priya (BlueHarbor): also need to confirm retention rules: can you support per-route retention windows and an on-demand purge API?
[03:59] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes per-route retention is supported. we also expose purge endpoints; for hosted we have an SLA'd purge timeline (e.g., purge acknowledged immediately, physical cleanup within X hours — we'll detail in SOW). for private you control purge timelines.
[04:18] Dana (BlueHarbor): how do you guarantee purge? audit logs? we need proof for auditors.
[04:24] Arjun (Redwood SE): we'll provide audit logs showing deletion events and a lineage log. for added assurance we can run a sample verification where we index hashes of prompts pre-delete and then show hashes are irretrievable post-delete. note: we'll include SOC 2/ISO artifacts in the packet.
[04:45] Marcus (BlueHarbor): KMS — is key material customer-managed?
[04:49] Arjun (Redwood SE): for hosted we support customer KMS (Bring Your Own Key) via our cloud integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure). for private it's your HSM/KMS. encryption at rest and in transit is standard.
[05:02] [Short silence / typing noise]
[05:12] Sofia (Redwood): ok shifting to benchmarks — Arjun can you walk through proposed workload sizing and metrics?
[05:18] Arjun (Redwood SE): sure. recommended approach for POC: two prompt families — 1) structured form family (highly templated, short context), 2) free-text support chat (longer, higher token variance). run 1,000 synthetic requests per family (2k total) across target model variants — we'll capture p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens per response, throughput qps, and per-1k-token cost estimate. also track cache hit rate if you use prefix caching.
[05:52] Dana (BlueHarbor): what's a realistic concurrency? our peak for the pilot is maybe 10 qps, burst to 50 during onboarding.
[06:00] Arjun (Redwood SE): that's fine. we'll simulate 10 sustained qps and short bursts to 50 in the bench harness. any specific token limits?
[06:08] Priya (BlueHarbor): some ID verification flows push up to 2k tokens per request but those will be rare. most are under 512.
[06:15] Arjun (Redwood SE): noted. we'll include a mix: 70% at 256 tokens, 25% at 512, 5% at 2k for the second prompt family.
[06:24] Marcus (BlueHarbor): how long does a bench run take? we have limited windows for testing in our staging.
[06:30] Arjun (Redwood SE): the 2k-run at 10 qps is about 200 seconds plus warmup and telemetry aggregation — we typically spin up for a 30–60 minute window including retries and traces.
[06:45] Dana (BlueHarbor): and will you provide a raw report + a summary sheet we can attach to the auditor?
[06:50] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes raw logs, summarized CSV with p50/p90/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and a redaction scorecard. we'll upload to the secure shared folder (we referenced the Redwood secure bench bucket). link sent after run.
[07:06] [timestamp roughness — lulls / microphone adjustments]
[07:20] Evan (BlueHarbor): procurement question — what does pricing look like for a 4-week pilot and what are cancellation terms?
[07:27] Sofia (Redwood): typical short pilot is a usage credit + small setup fee. i'll send a draft SOW. cancellation is straightforward; for hosted there's no long-term lock until you sign the Dedicated/Private contract.
[07:39] Priya (BlueHarbor): can we get explicit language for data residency — we need EU region processing for EU users.
[07:46] Arjun (Redwood SE): we can route requests to region-specific hosts and ensure data residency for those request routes. we'll add region routing to the SOW and config for the pilot.
[07:58] Dana (BlueHarbor): want to talk through an example flow — mortgage intake: prompt contains ssn, income, name. we want ssn redacted pre-send, income maybe masked, name ok to keep for context. can Redwood enforce per-field rules?
[08:12] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes per-field policies are doable. your pipeline can tag fields and call our sanitization lib which strips or masks per policy. alternatively you can send fields in structured payload and specify retention per field in route config.
[08:28] Marcus (BlueHarbor): curious about false negatives — if the sanitizer misses a variant of SSN how do we remediate?
[08:34] Arjun (Redwood SE): remediation options: 1) immediate purge on detection via purge API, 2) revoke any derived outputs, 3) for long-term we update patterns and re-scan logs if necessary. we'll include a documented incident playbook in the SOW.
[08:49] Sofia (Redwood): ok i want to capture success criteria verbatim for the POC doc. Dana can you confirm? list is: per-route retention enforced, redaction >= 99% on labeled test, p99 latency under X ms (we'll define X after bench), cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold, and audit artifacts delivered.
[09:09] Dana (BlueHarbor): yes that's our list. define X as part of the benchmark report.
[09:15] Arjun (Redwood SE): quick note on tooling: we have a bench harness that you'll run in your staging. it can use your keys and route to Redwood endpoints. results are collected into a CSV + Grafana snapshot. we'll share the harness repo and a how-to.
[09:32] Priya (BlueHarbor): are there any known limitations with quantized models or tokenization that could affect redaction? we've heard tokenization can split sensitive strings oddly.
[09:42] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes tokenization edge-cases do exist; for PII detection we run detection on the raw string before tokenization in the client-side sanitizer. on the server side we also map token boundaries for post-hoc redaction. we'll note that in the risk section.
[09:58] [ambient note: someone steps away briefly]
[10:04] Marcus (BlueHarbor): compliance-wise we need the list of people who will have access to raw logs. can you provide RBAC details?
[10:12] Sofia (Redwood): yes, Redwood provides RBAC and can limit access by role. we'll include a sample RBAC matrix in the security packet.
[10:20] Evan (BlueHarbor): quick on retention windows: do you do incremental purging (older than N days) or full-route tombstone? we want guaranteed removal for specific routes.
[10:29] Arjun (Redwood SE): both. you can configure time-based TTL per route and you can also trigger on-demand purge for a route or record set. tombstone semantics depend on deployment, but for hosted we guarantee physical deletion within the window described in the SOW.
[10:44] Dana (BlueHarbor): will the bench include a redaction efficacy test?
[10:48] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes; the labeled 500-sample test is part of the bench. we will run detection and report recall/precision and post-redaction leak examples (if any). we will redact any leaked content in the report.
[11:02] Priya (BlueHarbor): how do we handle 3rd-party integrations like logging exports to Splunk/Sumo? those endpoints could end up with PII if not careful.
[11:11] Arjun (Redwood SE): good point — we recommend disabling forwarding to external providers for the POC or enabling scrubbers before export. we can also set filters to suppress certain fields from telemetry exports.
[11:24] Sofia (Redwood): ok let's talk timeline: quick wins this week — Marcus shares redaction policy + sample PII, Priya confirms expected qps numbers, Sofia sends SOW. next week we run bench and then follow-up with results. are we aligned?
[11:38] Dana (BlueHarbor): yes aligned. one more ask — can we get a short runbook for incident response if PII leak is detected during the bench?
[11:46] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes we'll attach an incident playbook and example runbook to the security packet.
[11:53] [short cross talk / agreement sounds]
[12:00] Sofia (Redwood): recap of owners live: Arjun bench plan, Sofia SOW/pricing, Marcus redaction artifacts, Priya qps numbers, Evan coordinate schedule. we'll send calendar invites for bench window.
[12:16] Dana (BlueHarbor): thanks all. quick nit — we need to ensure the bench results include CPU/GPU metrics for the model runs for our infra team.
[12:25] Arjun (Redwood SE): we can include server-side resource metrics and approximate per-request GPU time. for hosted runs resource visibility is more limited but we provide effective throughput and token costs. for private we give full host metrics.
[12:40] Sofia (Redwood): sounds good. any final questions?
[12:44] Evan (BlueHarbor): none from me.
[12:46] Marcus (BlueHarbor): no.
[12:48] Priya (BlueHarbor): no.
[12:50] Dana (BlueHarbor): one small thing — can you include a sample purge API call syntax in the SOW?
[12:55] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes will include examples: curl + SDK snippet.
[13:02] Sofia (Redwood): great, we'll follow up with artifacts. thanks everyone.
